newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom agrees with Bonn on share sale.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom agrees with Bonn on share sale.

text.p: Deutsche Telekom AG has agreed a deal with the Bonn government that 25 percent of the remaning government-owned Telekom shares will be transfered to a state development agency, the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeiting said on Thursday.
The deal, which involves the state-owned agency Kredietanstalt fuer Wiederaufbua (KfW), would give Bonn a payout of 10 billion marks this year and 15 billion next, the report said.
The paper said Deutsche Telekom and the government would make a joint public statement on the deal later on Thursday.
Telekom is also due to hold its general meeting in Frankfurt on Thursday.
The government currently holds a 74-percent stake in Deutsch Telekom after 26 percent of the frim was privatised last November, raising 20 billion marks.

Bonn originally planned to keep the remaining stake until the year 2000, but has recently said it wants to speed up this and other privatisations to help boost public finances in the run up to European economic and monetary union (EMU).

While the government is prevented by law from selling any further Telekom shares onto the open market without the approval of Deutsche Telekom's board, the deal with KfW means the shares will be effectively "parked" with a state-owned agency, and their value will not be diluted.
